entries.reason: Pin-toggle and hide-column are 12px icon-slot affordances nested inside the sort-plumbed header cell (th carries the sort onClick/onKeyDown). Composing the DS Button primitive here would drag its chrome and focus-ring skin into the slot and fight the header's own interaction plumbing; the parts are skin-owned (data-table.css reset), keyboard-native, and mirror the grandfathered Carousel arrow/dot idiom.

ChartDataAccess (the isolated ./charts/access entrypoint) pins native buttons by contract: the tab-stop test asserts no .ds-button ancestor and the tab-order parts, and the entrypoint carries a 2800-byte gzip budget that the engine-switched Button cannot fit. The paint is skin-owned (chart-foundation data-trigger/data-action/data-pagination rules).
ChartDataAccess downloads the CSV through a detached anchor: a programmatic download is not presentation and has no primitive to move to.

The chart engine's tooltip div is a datum annotation positioned by chart geometry, not an interactive disclosure; role="tooltip" on a non-interactive element matches the ARIA pattern, and the accessible linkage IS wired: an active datum carries aria-describedby to the tooltip id (the per-type renderers, e.g. heat-map/index.tsx:261, line/index.tsx:343), pinned by SvgRenderers.test.tsx:521. No primitive host applies.

The chart tooltip is a datum annotation positioned by chart geometry, not an interactive disclosure; role="tooltip" on a non-interactive element matches the ARIA pattern. NOT VERIFIED: an accessible linkage from the chart to this tooltip is not demonstrated today (no aria-describedby from a focusable region measured); the annotation is visual-only until the chart accessibility layer proves the link — review then.
Chart export downloads the file through a detached anchor: a programmatic download is not presentation and has no primitive to move to.
The stats-grid sparkline is an owned data visualization (inline SVG by design, painted by the family skin); the graphics/icon facade covers semantic icons, not measured data ink.

The presence live-cursor glyph is a two-tone pattern-owned marker (per-user fill plus a surface-coloured outline the single-currentColor icon contract cannot express); no governed icon role fits it today. REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate the moment the semantic icon corpus admits a two-tone or collaboration role — this entry is not permanent by construction.

Sort activation lives on the th itself (sortable column header semantics: the sort button pattern keys aria-sort on the cell); nesting a DS Button in the header would fight the sort plumbing, mirroring the grandfathered icon-slot row of this same file.

TreeViewConnector is documented provider-free and server-safe, and the measured swap to NavLink breaks that contract (the engine-routed Link throws without a provider; 4 integration tests red when trialled). A static connector anchor is the correct element here.

The data-table rows (body rows via BodyRow, and the group-header row) are <tr> elements of the pattern's ARIA grid (role="grid" on the table, aria-rowindex/aria-colindex, td cells), which requires the native row element. No DS primitive renders a standalone <tr>: the Table primitive is a whole-table component with no compound row part and no exported row host, and this table's own row channel is the useStatefulPart props hook inside BodyRow, not an element host. Keyboard parity verified 2026-10-07: roving tabIndex (0/-1) on body rows, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End rove, Enter fires onRowClick, F2 opens the first editable cell; the group-header row is a tab stop that toggles on Enter/Space and carries aria-expanded. REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate if a grid-row host contract or the ARC-15 behaviour-core floor changes the element law; the exception covers the element choice, not the interaction quality.

The kanban BoardCard must be role="listitem" inside the column's role="list" and is both drag source and drop target of the shared sortable runtime (useDragSession getSourceProps/getTargetProps from primitives/runtime/collection/sortable); no DS primitive renders that role, and the sortable runtime, already composed here, is a props host rather than an element host. Keyboard parity verified 2026-10-07: the card is a tab stop (tabIndex 0, aria-roledescription), Enter/Space fire onItemClick through onActivate with the nested-control guard (a key on a control inside renderCard is ignored), the arrow-move protocol is the sortable runtime's immediate keyboard mode, and the coarse-pointer move rail uses real ModernButtons. REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate if the sortable runtime grows an item-host contract.

The CommandPaletteRow is an APG combobox role="option" carrying the option props of useComboboxFoundation (primitives/runtime/collection/combobox), the kernel that useListbox composes and through it Select, AutoComplete and Mentions. Focus stays on the role="combobox" input via aria-activedescendant by design, so a row is never DOM-focused (the kernel's option props carry no tabIndex) and the div's onClick is the pointer arm of the canonical pattern, not a reconstruction. No standalone Listbox/Option primitive exists to host it: Select.Option is a declarative data carrier that accepts only value/children/label/disabled/icon/className/style and cannot carry the kernel's id, aria-selected or handlers. REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate if proposal E-3 (Select render channel, pending owner) or a future Listbox/Option primitive lands.

The page-shell TabButton is a native <button role="tab"> by the Tabs-capability debrief of 2026-10-07 (G3 rejected the channel): the strip switches the page content area rendered outside the header, Tabs owns its panel and shares no tab/panel ids, and its panel-less strip mode carries no aria-controls, so adoption would either drop the measured tab-to-panel linkage or need an external-panel channel that publishes the Tabs id grammar and splits panel ownership for one consumer, which was rejected as not lawful-minimal. The native strip is APG-complete: a tablist named through i18n (pageShell.tabs.label, carried by the ar catalog), roving tabIndex, automatic activation, RTL-mirrored arrows, Home/End (PatternPageShell.modern-craft.test.tsx, including the ar locale case), real aria-controls/aria-labelledby linkage and the hideHeader guard that drops tabpanel semantics (PatternPageShell.modern-rescue.test.tsx). The exception comment sits above the tablist. REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate if Tabs lands an external-panel channel for a second consumer, or if the strip is reskinned onto the Tabs anatomy.

Same element as the page-shell TabButton native-button entry above (the role="tab" finding of the one <button>), under the same Tabs-capability debrief of 2026-10-07: Tabs owns its panel and its panel-less mode drops aria-controls, while this strip drives a content area outside the header with measured tab-to-panel linkage; keyboard parity is pinned by PatternPageShell.modern-craft.test.tsx and PatternPageShell.modern-rescue.test.tsx. REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate together with the native-button entry for this element.

The workbench-header SavedViewTab is a native <button role="tab"> (one element, carrying both the native-button and the role=tab finding). Tabs cannot express "no tab selected": it resolves activeKey ?? defaultActiveKey ?? firstSelectableKey(items) (tabs/engines/modern/index.tsx:396-407), and a no-selection state is a capability Tabs does not have (G4, Tabs-capability debrief 2026-10-07). The site's no-selection state is real: SavedViewTab carries aria-selected={isActive} and activeViewId may be undefined or name no view. Option (b), selecting the first view, was rejected because it misreports state. The strip is keyboard-complete in the selected state (roving tabIndex, automatic activation, RTL-mirrored arrows, Home/End) and reachable in the no-selection state: the first view holds the single tab stop while nothing is selected (WorkbenchHeader.modern-rescue.test.tsx). REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate when Tabs gains a no-selection state (G4) that keeps a single tab stop; the migration and this fix close together.

The calendar-view DayCell is a role="gridcell" of the pattern's APG month grid, and no DS primitive is a gridcell. The EventChip no longer shares this exception: it is hosted on the Button primitive with chrome="none" (EventChip trial 2026-10-07, GREEN: 21 protocol steps preserved in Chromium and WebKit, paint measured against the div chip). Keyboard parity of the cell, verified 2026-10-07: roving tabIndex on day cells, arrows move by day/week and mirror Left/Right under RTL, Enter/Space fire onDateClick, F2 enters the cell's first event chip. REVIEW CONDITION: re-evaluate when a calendar-cell host contract or the ARC-15 floor lands.
